title: Basel IRB Capital
vardeezReading: CR-10: Very Important. "Here, We can expect Different Credit Risk Models comparison to show up on exam. Don't get into Formulas too much here, but atleast know the details of each of 4 Models discussed here. Credit Spread Risk can be imp too." ORR-21: Untiered in the sheet, but his theme "Basel III: three components and comparison with Basel I and II" draws on this reading. ORR-23: Very Important. ORR-22: Untiered (tier cell reads 0), but his themes "Stressed market VaR (calculations)" and "Basel 2.5 market risk calculation" land squarely here, so treat as high priority.

selectors.name: IRB capital, single corporate loan
selectors.what: Capital (or RWA) for one corporate loan under Advanced IRB: WCDR = N((N^-1(PD) + sqrt(rho) x N^-1(0.999)) / sqrt(1 - rho)), with the wholesale correlation rho (0.12 to 0.24, falling as PD rises); Capital = EAD x LGD x (WCDR - PD) x MA; RWA = 12.5 x capital; MA from the maturity formula when M is given.
selectors.theory: Why capital covers unexpected loss only (the PD or EL term is subtracted from the 99.9th percentile default rate over one year); the asymptotic single risk factor (Gordy, one-factor Gaussian copula) logic under which each loan's capital depends only on its own PD, LGD and EAD; why corporate correlation falls as PD rises; why the maturity adjustment is largest for low-PD assets and applies to wholesale exposures only.

selectors.name: Retail IRB, fixed correlation, RWA
selectors.what: Capital or RWA for a retail exposure: the same WCDR formula with the fixed retail correlation (0.15 residential mortgages, 0.04 qualifying revolving, 0.03 to 0.16 formula for other retail) and no maturity adjustment, reported as RWA = 12.5 x EAD x LGD x (DR - PD).
selectors.theory: Why retail has no maturity adjustment, why retail correlations are lower than wholesale, and why the bank supplies its own PD, LGD and EAD (an Advanced-IRB-like treatment only).

selectors.name: Foundation versus Advanced IRB inputs
selectors.what: Which inputs the bank estimates and which the supervisor sets: Foundation IRB bank supplies PD only, with supervisory EAD, LGD (45% senior, 75% subordinated) and MA of 2.5, and a PD floor of 0.0003 for bank and corporate exposures; Advanced IRB bank supplies PD, LGD, EAD and MA; also the Basel II standardized approach and why IRB was expected to suit large banks.

selectors.name: December 2017 IRB revisions
selectors.what: What the December 2017 reforms changed in IRB: A-IRB removed for large and mid-sized corporates (revenues above EUR 500 million) and for banks and other financial institutions (to F-IRB or SA), all IRB removed for equities, input floors (PD floors under both approaches, LGD and EAD floors under A-IRB only), F-IRB senior unsecured LGD cut from 45% to 40%, the 1.06 scaling factor removed; also the motivation (restore credibility and comparability of RWAs).

selectors.name: The 72.5% output floor
selectors.what: RWA = max(RWA under approved approaches, 72.5% x RWA under the standardised approaches only); how the floor binds against modelled RWA, the approaches included in the floor base, the phase-in to 72.5% by 1 January 2027, and how input floors and the output floor differ.
selectors.theory: Why the output floor is a higher-of backstop and never a cap, why its base is standardised-only RWA at 72.5% (not modelled RWA, not 100% of standardised), and why it keeps a level playing field between modelled and standardised banks.

notSelected: CR-10 d beyond the Basel IRB use of Vasicek (the model comparison belongs to D20), ORR-21 e and f in their credit mitigant details (credit substitution, the 2005 double-default amendment) and the Large Exposure Framework, ORR-23 a beyond the IRB and output-floor motivation, and ORR-22 h (the post-crisis IRB changes, which repeat ORR-23 b) carry no separate shape, Map point or Vardeez pointer.
